# ClaimBack rulebook (authored by lead; do not edit wording without lead review)
Each rule: id | what the policyholder can assert | when it applies | source | confidence.
Only cite rules whose `applies_when` is supported by the documents. Never invent clauses.

R01 MORATORIUM_60M | After 60 continuous months of cover (ported/migrated years count), no health policy or claim can be contested for non-disclosure/misrepresentation, except established fraud. | Rejection cites non-disclosure / pre-existing disease / misrepresentation AND continuous cover >= 60 months. | IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29.05.2024 (IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024), Ch. I cl. 13 | high
R02 REJECTION_NEEDS_COMMITTEE_AND_CLAUSE | A claim may be rejected only with approval of the insurer's Product Management Committee or a 3-member Claims Review Committee, and the rejection letter must cite the specific policy terms relied on. | Rejection letter names no policy clause, or gives a vague reason ("not admissible", "as per policy terms"). | Health Master Circular 2024, Ch. I cl. 17 | high
R03 INSURER_COLLECTS_DOCUMENTS | Insurer/TPA must collect claim documents from the hospital; the policyholder should not be made to chase them. Claim should not be denied for missing hospital-held documents. | Rejection/query cites missing documents that the hospital holds (discharge summary, investigation reports, bills). | Health Master Circular 2024, Ch. I cl. 17(c) | high
R04 CASHLESS_1H_DISCHARGE_3H | Cashless requests must be decided within 1 hour; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours. Extra hospital charges caused by discharge delay are borne by the insurer (from shareholders' funds). | Cashless claim with delay in discharge authorisation and extra room/other charges billed for the delay. | Health Master Circular 2024, Ch. I cl. 15–16 | high
R05 DELAYED_INTIMATION_NOT_GROUND | A genuine claim cannot be rejected solely because of delay in intimation or document submission; insurer must consider reasons for delay. | Rejection reason is late intimation / late submission. | IRDA circular IRDA/HLTH/MISC/CIR/216/09/2011 (29.09.2011); NCDRC rulings applying it | high
R06 PROPORTIONATE_DEDUCTION_LIMITS | Proportionate deduction (for room above eligible category) may apply only to defined "associate medical expenses"; NEVER to pharmacy & consumables, implants & medical devices, diagnostics; NEVER to ICU charges; NEVER where hospital does not follow differential (room-based) billing for that item. | Settlement letter shows "proportionate deduction" applied to medicines, consumables, implants, diagnostics, ICU, or to items priced the same regardless of room. | IRDAI Modified Guidelines on Product Filing – Norms on Proportionate Deductions (2020), paras 3–7 | high
R07 SETTLEMENT_TIMELINE_INTEREST | Reimbursement (non-cashless) claims must be settled within 15 days of claim submission; if late, interest at bank rate + 2% p.a. is payable from receipt of claim intimation to payment. (Older 2020-standard wordings say 30 days from last necessary document, 45 days with investigation, same penal interest; the 2024 circular is the current IRDAI position.) | Reimbursement decision/payment came later than 15 days after submission. | IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 05.09.2024 (IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024); IRDAI Guidelines on Standardization in Health Insurance (penal interest clause) | high
R08 DAY_CARE_NOT_24H | Procedures that need under 24 hours because of technological advancement are day-care treatment; a claim cannot be rejected merely because hospitalisation was under 24 hours if the procedure is day-care or listed. | Rejection cites "hospitalisation less than 24 hours". | Policy day-care definition; consumer commission rulings (e.g. Ernakulam DCDRC 2023 intravitreal injections; Vadodara 2026 anaesthesia = day care) | medium
R09 MODERN_TREATMENTS | Insurers are expected to cover listed modern/technological treatments (e.g. oral chemotherapy, immunotherapy/monoclonal antibodies, robotic surgery, intravitreal injections, balloon sinuplasty, deep brain stimulation, uterine artery embolisation/HIFU, stem-cell therapy for haematological conditions). Check sub-limits in policy before asserting full payment. | Rejection says the treatment is "experimental"/"not covered" and it is in this list. | Health Master Circular 2024, Ch. I cl. 2 | medium
R10 AYUSH_PARITY | Insurers must have a board-approved policy to place AYUSH treatment on par with other systems of medicine. | AYUSH in-patient claim rejected or capped where policy wording covers AYUSH. | Health Master Circular 2024 Ch. I cl. 1(a)(iv); Insurance Products Regulations 2024 | medium
R11 PED_DEFINITION_36M | A pre-existing disease is only a condition diagnosed / treated within 36 months before the policy's first start date. Conditions diagnosed earlier than that window, or first diagnosed after the policy began, are not PED. Waiting periods for PED cannot exceed 36 months. | Rejection labels a condition PED where diagnosis evidence is outside the 36-month pre-policy window or after inception; or waiting period applied > 36 months. | IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024, definition of PED | high (definition); medium (36-month max waiting)
R12 NON_PAYABLE_ITEMS_ONLY_IF_LISTED | Deductions for "non-payable"/"non-medical" items must match the IRDAI standard excluded-items list (List I) and the policy. Items in Lists II–IV are meant to be subsumed into room, procedure or treatment charges — not deducted a second time when the hospital billed them inside a package. Some items are expressly payable (e.g. belts/braces after spine surgery). | Settlement shows deductions labelled "non-payable"/"NME"; check each against the list and whether the hospital billed a package. | IRDAI standardisation guidelines – list of excluded expenses (2013, carried into 2020 standardisation master circular Annexure) | medium
R13 MULTIPLE_POLICIES_CHOICE | With more than one indemnity policy, the policyholder chooses which to claim first; that insurer must then pursue the others for any balance. | Insurer refuses or delays because another policy exists. | Health Master Circular 2024, Ch. I cl. 18 | high
R14 OMBUDSMAN_ROUTE | Free complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman for claims up to ₹50 lakh, after a written complaint to the insurer is rejected / unanswered for 1 month / reply unsatisfactory; must be filed within 1 year of the insurer's reply; not while the same matter is in another court/forum. Award must be passed within 3 months of complete documents, is binding on the insurer, and must be complied with within 30 days, with interest. | Always the escalation path. | Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 (amended to 09.11.2023), Rules 14, 17; cioins.co.in | high
R15 GRIEVANCE_FIRST | First step is a written grievance to the insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer (also loggable on IRDAI Bima Bharosa portal). | Always step 1. | Ombudsman Rules 2017 r.14(3); IRDAI grievance framework | high

## Escalation timeline used by the tracker
Day 0: grievance to insurer GRO (+ Bima Bharosa). Day 15: reminder. Day 31 (no reply / rejected / unsatisfied): Insurance Ombudsman complaint (online via cioins.co.in), within 1 year of insurer reply. After award: insurer must pay within 30 days.

## Hard boundaries
- Output is a draft for the policyholder to send in their own name. ClaimBack does not appear before courts and does not give legal advice.
- If evidence suggests real non-disclosure inside 60 months or a genuine exclusion, say the case is WEAK. Never suggest hiding or altering facts.
